{{Short description|American wildlife biologist (born 1950)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2025}}

'''Thane Kastle Pratt''' (born 1950) is an American [[wildlife biologist]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://yalebooks.co.uk/book/9780300141085/conservation-biology-of-hawaiian-forest-birds/ |title=Conservation Biology of Hawaiian Forest Birds |date=2009 |publisher=[[Yale University Press]] |isbn=978-0-300-14108-5 |editor-last=Pratt |editor-first=Thane K. |pages=653–656 |chapter=Contributors |lccn=2009928176 |editor-last2=Atkinson |editor-first2=Carter T. |editor-last3=Banko |editor-first3=Paul C. |editor-last4=Jacobi |editor-first4=James D. |editor-last5=Woodworth |editor-first5=Bethany}}</ref> Pratt was raised in [[Hawaii]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |title=Akiapolaau: Hemignathus wilsoni |url=https://birdsoftheworld.org/bow/species/akiapo/cur/introduction |access-date=March 16, 2025 |website=Birds of the World |date=2024 |publisher=[[Cornell Lab of Ornithology]] |doi=10.2173/bow.akiapo.02 |language=en |last1=Pratt |first1=Thane K. |last2=Fancy |first2=Steven G. |last3=Ralph |first3=C. John |last4=Mlodinow |first4=Steven G. |last5=Pyle |first5=Peter |editor-first1=Nicholas D. |editor-last1=Sly }}</ref> and his research has focused on the birds of Hawaii and other Pacific islands. He led a career with the [[U.S. Geological Survey]] (USGS) until his 2009 retirement, and is the author of multiple books on the birds of Hawaii<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Bringing Extinction to Life |url=https://birdfesthawaii.org/bringing-extinction-to-life/ |access-date=March 16, 2025 |website= |publisher=[[Hawaiʻi Island Festival of Birds]] |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[New Guinea]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Pratt, Thane K. |url=https://press.princeton.edu/our-authors/pratt-thane-k |access-date=March 16, 2025 |website=Our Authors |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |language=en}}</ref> Pratt also serves as the regional editor for Hawaii and the Pacific islands in the [[Christmas Bird Count]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christmas Bird Count Regional Editors |url=https://www.audubon.org/conservation/christmas-bird-count-regional-compilers |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=Audubon |publisher=[[National Audubon Society]] |language=en}}</ref> A [[subspecies]] of ''[[Crateroscelis robusta]]'', ''C. r. pratti'', is named in his honor.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Engilis |first1=Andrew Jr. |last2=Cole |first2=Ronald E. |date=May 22, 1997 |title=Avifaunal Observations from the Bishop Museum Expedition to Mt. Dayman, Milne Bay Province, Papua New Guinea |url=http://hbs.bishopmuseum.org/pubs-online/pdf/op52.pdf |journal=Bishop Museum Occasional Papers |publisher=[[Bishop Museum Press]] |volume=52}}</ref> 

Pratt was born in [[Honolulu]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=Fall 2011 |title=Meet the Candidates! |url=https://fhvnp.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/02/2011.Fall_.pdf |journal=Newsletter |publisher=[[Friends of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park]] |pages=8 |access-date=March 15, 2025}}</ref> in 1950,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pratt, Thane K., 1950– [xx0261803] |url=https://aleph.nkp.cz/F/?func=find-c&local_base=aut&ccl_term=ica=xx0261803 |access-date=March 15, 2025 |website=Databases of the National Library CR |publisher=[[National Library of the Czech Republic]] |language=cs}}</ref> a son of John Scott Boyd Pratt III<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mair |first=Lynda |url=https://core.ac.uk/works/38553031/ |title=John Scott Boyd Pratt, III |date=1979 |publisher=[[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]] |series=Watumull Foundation Oral History Project |hdl=10524/48634 |access-date=March 15, 2025 |orig-date=October 15, 1971}}</ref> and Brenda ({{nee}} Cooke) Pratt.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2007 |title=Brenda Cooke Pratt |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/brenda-pratt-obituary?id=25270082 |access-date=March 15, 2025 |website=Legacy Remembers |publisher=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref> He attended [[Hawaii Preparatory Academy]], from which he graduated in 1969.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Supporters of HPA (2022–2023) |url=https://www.hpa.edu/annual-report-supporters/ |access-date=March 14, 2025 |publisher=[[Hawai‘i Preparatory Academy]] |quote=1660s ... Linda & Thane '69 Pratt}}</ref> During high school, he partook in [[birding]]; pages of his field notes dated 1967 are held in the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo]] research library.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Pratt |first=Thane K. |url=https://hilo.hawaii.edu/maunakea/library/ref/1624 |title=Field notes from Thane Pratt, Kamuela, Hawaii, post marked April 10, 1967 |date=1967 |volume=27 |pages=112–113}}</ref> Pratt holds a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree in biology and ecology from [[Colby College]], as well as a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in ecology from [[Rutgers University–New Brunswick]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

In 1986, the first edition of ''Birds of New Guinea'' by [[Bruce M. Beehler]], Pratt, and [[Dale A. Zimmerman]] was published by [[Princeton University Press]]. Described in an ''[[Australian Bird Watcher]]'' review as "a definitive field guide to the birds of New Guinea",<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Debus |first=Stephen |date=September 1987 |title=Birds of New Guinea [Book Review] |url=https://afo.birdlife.org.au/afo/index.php/afo/article/view/1008/983 |journal=[[Australian Bird Watcher]] |volume=12 |issue=3 |pages=103–105 |doi=10.3316/informit.600317086623140 <!-- As from https://search.informit.org/doi/10.3316/informit.600317086623140 --> |doi-broken-date=July 1, 2025}}</ref> the book contained text contributions and illustrations from multiple contributors.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Beehler |first1=Bruce M. |title=Birds of New Guinea |last2=Pratt |first2=Thane K. |last3=Zimmerman |first3=Dale A. |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |year=1986 |isbn=978-0-691-08385-8}}</ref> Another review, published in ''[[The Canadian Field-Naturalist]]'', described the book as a "worthwhile addition", but mentioned the lack of range maps.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=John |first=Roy |date=July–September 1997 |title=Birds of New Guinea, by Bruce M. Beehler, Thane K. Pratt, and Dale A. Zimmerman [Review] |journal=[[The Canadian Field-Naturalist]] |volume=101 |issue=3 |pages=499–500 |doi=10.5962/p.355970|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Beginning in 1989,<ref name=":0" /> Pratt was a wildlife biologist based at the U.S. Geological Survey's [[Pacific Island Ecosystems Research Center]] in [[Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park]]. As a researcher, his studies included bird population assessments of various Hawaiian islands. In 2009, the same year he retired from the USGS, ''Conservation Biology of Hawaiian Forest Birds'', an [[edited book]] by Pratt and coeditors, was published by [[Yale University Press]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://yalebooks.co.uk/book/9780300141085/conservation-biology-of-hawaiian-forest-birds/ |title=Conservation Biology of Hawaiian Forest Birds |date=2009 |publisher=[[Yale University Press]] |isbn=978-0-300-14108-5 |editor-last=Pratt |editor-first=Thane K. |lccn=2009928176 |editor-last2=Atkinson |editor-first2=Carter T. |editor-last3=Banko |editor-first3=Paul C. |editor-last4=Jacobi |editor-first4=James D. |editor-last5=Woodworth |editor-first5=Bethany}}</ref> The book, considered the culmination of his USGS research projects,<ref name=":1" /> was described as "excellent" in a review published by ''[[The Auk]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=van Riper |first=Charles III |date=2010-10-01 |title=Conservation Biology of Hawaiian Forest Birds: Implications for Island Avifauna |journal=[[The Auk]] |volume=127 |issue=4 |pages=956–958 |doi=10.1525/auk.2010.127.4.956}}</ref> and received an additional positive review in ''[[The Condor (journal)|The Condor]]''. The latter review noted the book's "depressing" tone and urged politicians to further support the research described in the volume.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Steadman |first=David W. |date=2010-11-01 |title=Conservation Biology of Hawaiian Forest Birds: Implications for Island Avifauna |journal=[[The Condor (journal)|The Condor]] |volume=112 |issue=4 |pages=863–864 |doi=10.1525/cond.2010.112.4.863}}</ref>

Two new editions of ''Birds of New Guinea'' (a second and revised edition), now edited by Pratt and Beehler,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bishop |first=David |date=2017-08-30 |title=A New Look at New Guinea |url=https://blog.aba.org/2017/08/a-new-look-at-new-guinea.html |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=ABA Blog |publisher=[[American Birding Association]] |language=en-US}}</ref> were published by [[Princeton University Press]] between 2014 and 2016.<ref name=":3" /> Reviews for the edition were published in ''The Canadian Field-Naturalist'',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=John |first=Roy |date=January–March 2015 |title="Birds of New Guinea: Second Edition" by T.K. Pratt & B.M. Beehler. 2015. [book review] |journal=[[The Canadian Field-Naturalist]] |language=en |volume=129 |issue=1 |pages=99 |doi=10.22621/cfn.v129i1.1677}}</ref> ''[[Ibis (journal)|Ibis]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal |date=July 2015 |title=Book reviews |journal=[[Ibis (journal)|Ibis]] |language=en |volume=157 |issue=3 |pages=652–666 |doi=10.1111/ibi.12277}}</ref> and the ''[[Journal of Field Ornithology]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mack |first=Andrew L. |date=June 2015 |title=Birds of New Guinea, Second Edition |journal=[[Journal of Field Ornithology]] |language=en |volume=86 |issue=2 |pages=189–190 |doi=10.1111/jofo.12104}}</ref>
